messages:
acme.ops: Hey team — after the canary we rolled earlier today our chatbot is returning old onboarding templates for ~10% of users. Example: user asked for 'pricing tiers' and got the legacy tier text from last month, not the updated content we pushed. This started ~5m after the deploy. Can you help?

maria (Support): Sorry about that — can you paste a full request/response (or request id) so we can trace? Any customer id / prompt you can share safely?

acme.ops: Sure. Request id: r-2026-03-17-42. Repro curl: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2b","prompt":"Show onboarding pricing tiers for AcmeCo","metadata":{"template_id":"pricing_v2","user_id":"u123"}}'``` Response (truncated): ```{"id":"r-2026-03-17-42","output":"Legacy pricing: Starter - $5...","model":"redwood-2b","cache_prefix":"tpl:pricing:hash_abc123"}```

maria (Support): Thanks. That cache_prefix is interesting. @Raj can you take a look?

Raj (Eng): Looking. From the logs r-2026-03-17-42 hits a KV prefix entry created earlier (tpl:pricing:hash_abc123) at 2026-03-17T10:12:01Z. The template content for pricing_v2 was updated and the canary created a new template key, but I see some requests still routing to the older prefix on the canary nodes.

Eli (Oncall): deploy-bot shows canary rollout started at 2026-03-17T10:10:48Z -> 20% nodes, then 60% at 10:11:30Z. There's an autoscaler spin at 10:12 that added ephemeral instances. Possible stale KV state on those ephemeral instances.

Raj (Eng): Hypothesis: prefix naming changed semantics during the template migrate, and older nodes still had the old prefix mapping in local KV cache. If routing hits a node with stale local prefix entries, requests get old output from prefix lookup.

maria (Support): Any quick mitigation we can ask the customer to do while you debug?

Raj (Eng): Two quick options: 1) For immediate customer-facing mitigation, re-run the request with a cache_bust header so it bypasses prefix lookup: `X-RW-Cache: no-prefix` — that'll force compute and return fresh output. 2) On infra side, roll a targeted invalidate for tpl:pricing:* across KV ring. I'll run an invalidate and follow up.

maria (Support): Sharing the cache_bust header to Acme now. Also asking if they can repro with a new request id (so we can see a no-cache trace).

acme.ops: Trying header now... curl with `-H 'X-RW-Cache: no-prefix'` returned the updated pricing_v2 payload. Thanks. We can use that as a workaround but need root cause.

Raj (Eng): I'm running `kv.invalidate(prefix="tpl:pricing:")` across the cluster. I see inconsistent prefix state: some nodes still have hash_abc123 (old template) pinned in local prefix cache for up to 6 hours. Root cause probable race during template migration when we changed prefix hashing function — some canary instances built prefixes with older hash seeds.

Eli (Oncall): Noted. I'm pinning an oncall ticket and increasing the KV prefix eviction frequency as a short term fix. Also disabling prefix caching on newly provisioned ephemeral nodes until hash rotation finishes.

maria (Support): Customer confirms incidence rate dropped to ~0.5% after invalidation. They're okay with roll-forward but worried about recurrence.

Raj (Eng): Action items: 1) Reconcile hashing seeds across service images (in progress). 2) Add a migration step to explicitly recompute and repopulate prefix keys after template deploys. 3) Add metric to detect prefix collisions (prefix_id -> template_id drift). 4) Postmortem and a preflight check in canary to validate prefix parity.

deploy-bot: Candidate rollback scheduled? No rollback triggered (canary threshold not breached).

maria (Support): I'll update the customer with the workaround and ETA for fix. Thanks all. :handshake:

Raj (Eng): I'll follow up with a quick runbook for oncall: how to invalidate prefixes, how to force-bypass cache, and how to detect drift.

Eli (Oncall): Marking this as P2 for now, will escalate to P1 if user visible error > 5% or 30 min sustained.

maria (Support): Closing loop once we have the postmortem. If Acme has more repro cases I'll collect request ids and paste here.

acme.ops: Thanks team, appreciate the quick response.
